name: Modern Life Is War
label: Deathwish
lede: Five friends from Marshalltown, Iowa, a 27-minute record with an 1896 photo of their own Main Street on the cover, and a band that quit, came back and kept writing about home.

eras.title: A seven-inch and a sixteen-date tour
eras.text: Modern Life Is War starts in Marshalltown, Iowa, in 2002 with a 7-inch and a tour the band books itself. A label rep sees them on the road and offers a full-length.

years.h: Marshalltown friends put out a self-titled 7-inch
years.p: [[Jeffrey Eaton|1ba65c8b-4014-4d4a-bb09-dbff3e4c5d55]] is recruited by childhood friends to front their hardcore band. The 7-inch was recorded in a church choir studio in Iowa, according to Eaton.
years.xp:
Eaton told Punknews.org he came to hardcore through a Rancid video on MTV in eighth grade, and that Gorilla Biscuits' Start Today was the first hardcore record he loved. The band was [[Jeffrey Eaton|1ba65c8b-4014-4d4a-bb09-dbff3e4c5d55]], guitarists John Eich and Matt Hoffman, bassist Chris Honeck and drummer Tyler Oleson.

Wikipedia lists the 7-inch on Lifeline Records.

years.h: They book a 16-date tour by mailing out 100 copies of the 7-inch
years.p: The band sent the 7-inch to promoters across the country and offered to open shows for 15 minutes for free. It worked well enough to fill a tour with [[Champion|744cff3e-33b3-4f1c-b703-84aea4d811f7]], The Hope Conspiracy and Black Widows.
years.xp: Eaton told Punknews.org that a Martyr Records representative saw them on that first tour and offered a full-length deal.

years.h: My Love. My Way. recorded in Brooklyn
years.p: The debut LP was recorded in March 2003 at Atomic Recording Company in Brooklyn, New York, and runs about 24 minutes over ten tracks.
years.xp: Wikipedia credits the release to Martyr Records. Its band page lists Lifeline Records for the album. [[Jacob Bannon|d5c2a3e1-a52a-4af6-8e3f-aa2c4dc69af7]] of [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]] co-directed the art with Christopher Cannon, and Deathwish Inc. later handled reissues, including a remaster with two bonus tracks from the 7-inch.

eras.title: Deathwish and a photo of Main Street
eras.text: Bannon's new label puts out Witness. Two founding members leave right after it is finished.

years.p: Recorded at Volume in Chicago and God City in Massachusetts, with [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]] mixing. It runs about 27 minutes.
years.xp: Mastering was by Alan Douches. Punknews.org ranked it fifth on its year-end list and wrote that if every album could be like it, "maybe music wouldn't suck as bad."

years.cap: Witness cover art by Jacob Bannon
years.h: Bannon puts Marshalltown's 1896 Main Street on the cover
years.p: [[Jacob Bannon|d5c2a3e1-a52a-4af6-8e3f-aa2c4dc69af7]] designed the Witness sleeve around an 1896 photograph of Main Street in the band's hometown of Marshalltown, Iowa.
years.xp: Bannon runs Deathwish Inc. and fronts [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]]. Sputnik Music gave the album five stars and called it "quite possibly the greatest hardcore album of our generation."

years.h: Matt Hoffman and Chris Honeck leave; Sjarm 13 and Tim Churchman join
years.p: The two exits come right after Witness. Sjarm 13 takes over guitar and Churchman bass, per Wikipedia.
years.xp: Eaton later told Punknews.org that Hoffman and Honeck left at different points, and that he felt the band's non-stop pace burned them out.

eras.title: Midnight in America and the end
eras.text: A new line-up makes a record with J. Robbins, then calls it quits in a MySpace post.

years.p: [[J. Robbins|3babd931-a940-43a8-b629-d7aed5b821d9]] produced the band's third album for Equal Vision Records, out August 21, 2007. It includes a cover of the folk song "Stagger Lee."
years.xp: Alan Douches mastered it. Stylus Magazine gave it an A-. The line-up was Eaton, Eich, Sjarm 13, Churchman and Oleson.

years.big: Six years of nonstop touring, then a MySpace post
q: I wish we took a break or six months off.
years.h: Modern Life Is War announce their breakup on MySpace
years.p: The band called it on February 19, 2008, after three albums and a run of EPs and tours.
years.xp: Eaton later told Punknews.org that the constant push burned them out and that he wished the band had taken a break instead of splitting.

years.h: "Fuck the Sex Pistols" gets a video
years.p: The 2008 clip for the Midnight in America song arrives around the breakup.

eras.title: Chris asks, and the basement fills up
eras.text: Honeck starts the reunion talk. The original five write a record in John Eich's basement.

years.h: Chris Honeck asks to reunite, and Eaton sets one condition
years.p: Honeck raised it in March 2012. Eaton said he would only do it if they all wrote a new record together.
years.xp:
Eaton told Punknews.org that Honeck had to play bass or it would not feel like Modern Life Is War. Between the breakup and the reunion Eaton had moved to California and made his living DJing soul, funk, reggae and ska records.

Wikipedia says writing began in September 2012 in Eich's basement.

years.h: Reunion announced; first show is This Is Hardcore in Philadelphia
years.p: Promoter Joe Hardcore had invited them to play the festival, their first show in five years. Wikipedia says it and a record release show were all that was booked at first.

The first record in six years is engineered and mixed by [[Kurt Ballou|1e922902-2cb9-499f-aeb5-9a8c51dd0df0]] at his God City studio, out September 9, 2013 on Deathwish Inc. It has 11 tracks and runs about 31 minutes.
years.xp: Brad Boatright mastered it. Metacritic lists 81/100, Pitchfork gave it 7.9. Release shows in October hit Iowa, Chicago, Washington DC, New York and Boston.

eras.title: Ten years of Witness and three Tribulation records
eras.text: The band reissues its landmark record, then puts out short releases on their own schedule.

years.p: Deathwish Inc. puts out a remastered Witness with new packaging and liner notes, followed by a nine-date North American tour.
Two EPs arrive in 2018 alongside a video for "Feels Like End Times."

years.h: Tribulation Work Songs Vol. 3 and a video for "Survival"
years.p: The third volume comes out in 2021, with a clip for "Survival."

eras.title: Life on the Moon
eras.text: A fifth album, twelve years after Fever Hunting.

years.h: Life on the Moon, their first album in 12 years
years.p: Out September 5, 2025 via Deathwish Inc. and Iodine Recordings. First single "Johnny Gone" came in June.
years.xp: Deathwish describes the album as made over several years with longtime collaborator Brooks Strause, and as dealing with loss and grief. Eaton described "Johnny Gone" as being about obsolescence and activism, touching on East Palestine, Ohio and Tehran, Iran.
